findings.body:
Removing the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check means `deliver()` will POST to any caller-supplied URL via `urllib.request.urlopen` with no scheme, host, or network-range validation.

**Failure mode:** a customer- or attacker-controlled `url` such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `http://127.0.0.1:2375/`, or an internal hostname reaches the runner/network from this process. Default redirect following can also pivot from a public endpoint to a private one.

**Fix:** keep an explicit allowlist or equivalent safe-URL policy before opening the request — at minimum HTTPS-only, block loopback/link-local/private CIDRs and metadata addresses, resolve DNS and re-check the resolved IP, and disable or tightly control redirects. Restore a host allowlist (or per-tenant configured HTTPS endpoints validated at save time and again at delivery) rather than posting to an arbitrary string.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only host allowlist on outbound webhook delivery and turns `deliver()` into an open SSRF primitive.

## What changed

`webhooks.py` deleted `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the `urlsplit` hostname check, then posts the caller-supplied `url` straight through `urllib.request.urlopen`. The PR frames this as supporting customer-configured endpoints; that product goal needs an allowlist, HTTPS-only policy, and private/link-local/metadata IP blocking — not an unrestricted fetch.

## Why it matters

Any value that reaches `deliver(..., url)` can hit:

- Cloud metadata (`http://169.254.169.254/…`)
- Localhost and RFC1918 admin panels
- Internal hooks the old allowlist was meant to fence

`urllib.request` follows redirects by default, so a public URL can still bounce onto an internal target. Timeout alone does not bound blast radius.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes the ALLOWED_HOSTS check that previously rejected non-allowlisted hosts before urllib.request.urlopen; deliver() now POSTs to any caller-supplied URL with no scheme/host/IP validation, enabling classic SSRF (metadata, loopback, internal hosts). Critical severity is appropriate.
